Testing shows how your AI responds to adversarial inputs, manipulation attempts, control bypasses, data extraction techniques and other attack scenarios. Unlike many AI red teaming service providers that stop at prompt testing, Folio3 tests the full chain: applications, workflows, integrations and the controls around them.
The goal is simple:
Simulate the attack, expose the weakness and strengthen the defense.

settings.editor: AI red teaming services simulate adversarial attacks against AI applications and workflows to find exploitable weaknesses and test how well your security controls work.
AI red teaming focuses on AI-specific attack scenarios, including manipulating AI behavior, adversarial inputs, data extraction and AI workflow risks.
Scope can include prompt injection, jailbreaks, data extraction, workflow manipulation, application attacks and other relevant adversarial scenarios.
Yes. Existing AI applications and workflows can be tested to find current weaknesses and see how controls respond to adversarial activity.
Yes. Testing can cover AI workflows, integrations, APIs, tools and connected systems within the agreed scope.
Scope and test environments are agreed before testing begins, with boundaries set around your application’s architecture and operational needs.
Findings are validated and prioritized, followed by practical recommendations to fix vulnerabilities and strengthen AI security controls.
